checkpoint_2.owner_concern: Recurring small-slice refactor pattern: a code-duplication/ownership-misplacement signal is sunk to a canonical layer, proven via before/after structural (ArchGuard-shaped) comparison plus a constructed negative control and a branch-self-host code-identity proof, then merged as exactly one commit under explicit human activation.

owned_mechanisms_or_paths: goal-branch ownership-first refactor slices (destination layer unspecified at this checkpoint)

checkpoint_2.note: Synthesized from boolean feature vectors ONLY (per task constraint) — negative_control and human_activated differed between GOAL-030/031, so this contract omits any claim both are universal; omitted entirely is WHICH layer things sink to (e.g. "kernel") and WHAT domain each slice covers, since the feature vector has no field for that — those would require relaxing the prose-free constraint.

checkpoint_3.owner_concern: Same concern as checkpoint 2, reconfirmed by a third independent sample (GOAL-032): a code-duplication/ownership-misplacement signal sunk to a canonical layer, proven via before/after structural comparison, a negative control, and branch-self-host identity, merged as exactly one commit under explicit human activation.
checkpoint_3.note: GOAL-030 and GOAL-032 agree on all 9/9 extracted features (perfect match); GOAL-031 still differs on negative_control and human_activated.
